LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard AUR packaging constructs that are safe to evaluate during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. At the top level (global scope), the file performs: variable assignments (pkgbase, pkgver, source arrays, checksums), a benign command substitution for `_basever` using grep/printf, exports of KBUILD environment variables using a `date` call, function definitions (prepare, build, _package variants), and a for-loop with `eval` that wraps `_package*` functions into `package*` functions. None of these operations download or execute untrusted code, exfiltrate data, or perform dangerous system modifications. The `eval` loop merely captures function definitions via `declare -f` and creates wrapper functions — it does not invoke the function bodies. All `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` function bodies are out of scope for this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>No malicious code detected in top-level scope of PKGBUILD</summary>
</security_assessment>
